From 6b470f36616e3448d44b0ef4b1de2a3e3a31b5be Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Date: Mon, 8 Dec 2025 19:54:08 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] wifi: mt76: Fix memory leak destroying device

All MT76 rx queues have an associated page_pool even if the queue is not
associated to a NAPI (e.g. WED RRO queues with WED enabled). Destroy the
page_pool running mt76_dma_cleanup routine during module unload.
Moreover returns pages to the page pool if WED is not enabled for WED RRO
queues.

Fixes: 950d0abb5cd94 ("wifi: mt76: mt7996: add wed rx support")
Signed-off-by: Lorenzo Bianconi <lorenzo@kernel.org>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251208-mt76-fix-memory-leak-v1-1-cba813fc62b8@kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Felix Fietkau <nbd@nbd.name>

diff --git a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c
index f240016ed9f0..893ac14285ca 100644
--- a/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c
+++ b/drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c
@@ -874,7 +874,12 @@ mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(struct mt76_dev *dev, struct mt76_queue *q)
 		if (!buf)
 			break;
 
-		if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q))
+		if (mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) &&
+		    mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q))
+			continue;
+
+		if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_rxdmad_c(q) &&
+		    !mt76_queue_is_wed_rro_ind(q))
 			mt76_put_page_pool_buf(buf, false);
 	} while (1);
 
@@ -1168,10 +1173,6 @@ void mt76_dma_cleanup(struct mt76_dev *dev)
 	mt76_for_each_q_rx(dev, i) {
 		struct mt76_queue *q = &dev->q_rx[i];
 
-		if (mtk_wed_device_active(&dev->mmio.wed) &&
-		    mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q))
-			continue;
-
 		netif_napi_del(&dev->napi[i]);
 		mt76_dma_rx_cleanup(dev, q);
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `drivers/net/wireless/mediatek/mt76/dma.c`

**1. `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup` function**  
- **Before:** The condition `if (!mt76_queue_is_wed_rro(q))` caused all WED RRO queues to skip returning page pool buffers, regardless of whether WED was active.  
- **After:** The logic is refined:  
  - If WED is active AND the queue is a WED RRO queue, the buffer is skipped (WED manages the pages).  
  - Otherwise, the buffer is returned to the page pool, **except** for two specific sub‑types of WED RRO queues (`WED_RRO_RXDMAD_C` and `WED_RRO_IND`). This ensures that when WED is not enabled, pages used by other WED RRO queues are properly returned.

**2. `mt76_dma_cleanup` function**  
- **Before:** There was an explicit skip that prevented `netif_napi_del` and `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup` from being called for WED RRO queues when WED was active.  
- **After:** That skip is removed, so **all** RX queues (including WED RRO queues) now undergo cleanup. This ensures that the page pools associated with those queues are destroyed during driver unload.

### Relationships Between Changes
- The removal of the skip in `mt76_dma_cleanup` guarantees that the `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup` routine is executed for every queue, including WED RRO queues.  
- The refined conditions inside `mt76_dma_rx_cleanup` then correctly decide when to return page pool buffers, preventing both memory leaks (by destroying unused page pools) and premature page release (when WED is actively managing those queues).  
- Together, these two changes fix the memory leak that occurred when destroying the device: previously, page pools for WED RRO queues were never cleaned up, and pages could be lost if WED was not active.
